---
title: "DC vehicle taxes: a 5% value tax over $40k, a length surcharge, and a hood-height surcharge"
output: html_document
---

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(readxl)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)
options(scipen = 999, width = 110, pillar.sigfig = 6)

dmv_file  <- "dmv_data_cleaned.csv"  # cleaned DMV new-registration data
len_file  <- "vehicle_lengths.csv"   # lengths of nameplates longer than a Camry (built for this note)
hood_file <- "hood_heights_v4.xlsx"  # hood leading-edge heights, 195 nameplates (carsized.com photos)
stock     <- 279262                  # DC household vehicles, ACS 2020-24 (B25046)

# ---- Part 1: value tax settings -------------------------------------------
rate      <- 0.05                    # value tax rate
threshold <- 40000                   # value tax applies to value above this
spread    <- 0.30                    # log-sd of prices within a brand

# ---- Part 2: length surcharge settings (edit these, then re-knit) ----------
fee_at_esv <- 300          # annual fee ($) for a vehicle as long as a 2025 Escalade ESV
curve      <- 1            # 1 = fee rises linearly with length; 2 = quadratic
fee_cap    <- fee_at_esv   # top fee ($) in the "capped" results; or type a dollar amount
L_camry    <- 193.5        # fee starts above this length (in.): 2025 Toyota Camry
L_esv      <- 227.0        # fee reaches fee_at_esv at this length (in.): 2025 Escalade ESV
commercial_types <- c("Van", "Heavy-duty pickup")  # vehicle types exempted as "commercial"
ext_share  <- 1/3          # share of lumped SUVs that are the long version (ESV, Expedition MAX, ...)

# ---- Part 3: hood-height surcharge settings (edit these, then re-knit) -----
hood_fee_at_esv <- 300               # annual fee ($) at the hood height of a Cadillac Escalade ESV
hood_curve      <- 1                 # 1 = fee rises linearly with hood height; 2 = quadratic
hood_fee_cap    <- hood_fee_at_esv   # top fee ($) in the "capped" results; or type a dollar amount
H_low           <- 35                # fee starts above this hood height (in.)
H_high          <- 45                # fee reaches hood_fee_at_esv here (in.): Cadillac Escalade, from hood_file
H_hd_pickup     <- 55                # assumed hood height (in.) of heavy-duty pickups, which weren't measured
```

# Part 1. A 5% tax on vehicle value over $40,000

## 1. Prices when new

Kelley Blue Book average transaction prices by brand, October 2026. Brands not in the KBB table get rough guesses.

```{r prices}
atp <- c(ACURA = 50320, AUDI = 64403, BMW = 73149, BUICK = 37400, CADILLAC = 90101,
         CHEVROLET = 51058, CHRYSLER = 49959, DODGE = 53475, FORD = 61565, GENESIS = 64316,
         GMC = 65607, HONDA = 38198, HYUNDAI = 38320, INFINITI = 69865, JEEP = 53592,
         KIA = 39260, `LAND ROVER` = 102826, LEXUS = 63899, LINCOLN = 78132, MAZDA = 37082,
         MERCEDESBENZ = 71086, MINI = 41075, MITSUBISHI = 33579, NISSAN = 37578,
         PORSCHE = 125270, RAM = 69850, SUBARU = 37429, TESLA = 54194, TOYOTA = 44168,
         VOLKSWAGEN = 40185, VOLVO = 61588)
guesses <- c(JAGUAR = 70000, `ALFA ROMEO` = 50000, MASERATI = 100000, POLESTAR = 60000,
             LUCID = 90000, RIVIAN = 85000, FIAT = 30000, SMART = 25000, ASTONMARTIN = 250000,
             FERRARI = 250000, BENTLEY = 250000, LAMBORGHINI = 250000, ROLLSROYCE = 250000,
             `ROLLS ROYCE` = 250000, MCLAREN = 250000, MERCURY = 30000, PONTIAC = 30000,
             SATURN = 30000, SAAB = 35000, OLDSMOBILE = 30000, HUMMER = 60000, SCION = 25000,
             ISUZU = 35000, PLYMOUTH = 25000)
price_new <- c(atp, guesses)

# Industry average new price by model year (approximate), used to scale older cars back.
# Anchors: KBB put the 2018 average near $36,000 and October 2026 at $51,109.
atp_year <- c(`2015` = 33500, `2016` = 34500, `2017` = 35500, `2018` = 36500, `2019` = 37800,
              `2020` = 40000, `2021` = 45000, `2022` = 48500, `2023` = 48500, `2024` = 48500,
              `2025` = 49800, `2026` = 51109)
```

## 2. Which cars are still registered in DC

The DMV file counts cars *first registered* in DC each year. Assuming a constant share stays registered each year, that share is 1 − (2025 registrations ÷ total cars).

```{r stock}
dmv <- read_csv(dmv_file, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(weight_class %in% c("Class I", "Class II", "Class III"),
         make_clean %in% names(price_new))

inflow_2025 <- sum(dmv$n[dmv$year == 2025])
retention   <- 1 - inflow_2025 / stock

dmv <- dmv |> mutate(still_here = n * retention^(2025 - year))

c(inflow_2025 = inflow_2025, retention = round(retention, 3),
  modeled_stock = round(sum(dmv$still_here)))
```

## 3. Value today

Depreciation follows Kelley Blue Book's average rates for years 1–5 (16%, 12%, 11%, 9%, 7%), then 7% a year after that.

```{r value}
dep_rates  <- c(0.16, 0.12, 0.11, 0.09, rep(0.07, 150))  # long enough for 1920s cars
dep_factor <- c(1, cumprod(1 - dep_rates))   # share of value left at age 0, 1, 2, ...

scale_to_year <- function(my) {
  ifelse(my < 2015, 33500 / 51109 * 0.97^(2015 - my),
         atp_year[as.character(pmin(pmax(my, 2015), 2026))] / 51109)
}

dmv <- dmv |>
  mutate(age   = pmax(2025 - model_year, 0),
         value = unname(price_new[make_clean]) * scale_to_year(model_year) * dep_factor[age + 1])
```

## 4. Tax per car

Prices vary within a brand (a "Toyota" can be a $25k Corolla or a $75k Sequoia), so each brand-year's value is treated as the average of a lognormal distribution. The expected tax is then 5% of the expected amount above $40k.

```{r tax}
expected_excess <- function(mu, k = threshold, s = spread) {
  d1 <- (log(mu / k) + s^2 / 2) / s
  mu * pnorm(d1) - k * pnorm(d1 - s)
}
share_over <- function(mu, k = threshold, s = spread) pnorm((log(mu / k) + s^2 / 2) / s - s)

dmv <- dmv |>
  mutate(tax     = rate * expected_excess(value),
         p_taxed = share_over(value))
```

## Results

```{r results}
total <- dmv |> summarise(cars          = sum(still_here),
                          cars_taxed    = sum(still_here * p_taxed),
                          revenue_M     = sum(still_here * tax) / 1e6,
                          avg_tax_taxed = sum(still_here * tax) / sum(still_here * p_taxed))
round(total, 1)

dmv |>
  mutate(age_group = cut(age, c(-1, 0, 2, 5, 9, Inf),
                         labels = c("New", "1-2", "3-5", "6-9", "10+"))) |>
  group_by(age_group) |>
  summarise(cars       = round(sum(still_here)),
            cars_taxed = round(sum(still_here * p_taxed)),
            revenue_M  = round(sum(still_here * tax) / 1e6, 1))
```

## Sensitivity

```{r sensitivity}
run <- function(s = spread, scale_back = TRUE) {
  v <- unname(price_new[dmv$make_clean]) * dep_factor[dmv$age + 1] *
       (if (scale_back) scale_to_year(dmv$model_year) else 1)
  ex <- if (s == 0) pmax(v - threshold, 0) else expected_excess(v, s = s)
  round(sum(dmv$still_here * rate * ex) / 1e6, 1)
}

tibble(variant   = c("Brand averages only (no spread)", "Central (spread 0.3)",
                     "Wider spread (0.4)", "Today's prices for all model years"),
       revenue_M = c(run(s = 0), run(), run(s = 0.4), run(scale_back = FALSE)))
```

# Part 2. An annual length surcharge

The surcharge is \$0 for a vehicle no longer than a 2025 Toyota Camry (`r L_camry` in.). Above that it rises `r if (curve == 1) "in a straight line" else paste0("with the extra length raised to the power ", curve)`, reaching $`r fee_at_esv` at the length of a 2025 Cadillac Escalade ESV (`r L_esv` in.) and continuing upward beyond it. The "capped" results stop it at $`r fee_cap`. All of these settings live in the `setup` chunk at the top.

## 5. The schedule

```{r schedule}
surcharge <- function(len, cap = Inf) {
  pmin(fee_at_esv * (pmax(len - L_camry, 0) / (L_esv - L_camry))^curve, cap)
}

tribble(~vehicle,                           ~length_in,
        "Toyota Camry (2025)",              193.5,
        "Toyota Highlander (2020+)",        194.9,
        "Ford Explorer (2020+)",            198.8,
        "Toyota Sienna (2021+)",            203.7,
        "Chevrolet Tahoe (2021+)",          210.7,
        "Toyota Tacoma Double Cab (2024+)", 213.0,
        "Chevrolet Suburban (2021+)",       225.7,
        "Cadillac Escalade ESV (2021+)",    227.0,
        "Ford F-150 SuperCrew, 5.5 ft box", 231.7,
        "Ram ProMaster, 159 in. wheelbase", 236.2,
        "Ford Transit, extended length",    263.9) |>
  mutate(uncapped = round(surcharge(length_in)),
         capped   = round(surcharge(length_in, cap = fee_cap)))
```

## 6. Vehicle lengths

The DMV file has make, model and model year, but not trim, cab or wheelbase. `vehicle_lengths.csv` gives an overall length, one row per generation, for every nameplate longer than a Camry among those with five or more 2025 registrations (97% of vehicles), plus rarer big trucks, vans and SUVs. Anything not listed is treated as Camry-length or shorter. Two simplifications:

* **Pickups and vans** get their most common body (crew cab with short bed; 148-in. Transit; 159-in. ProMaster). Their shortest and longest bodies feed the sensitivity check.
* **Extended-length SUVs.** The DMV lumps some SUVs with their extended versions: Escalade ESV, Expedition MAX, Navigator L, Wagoneer L, Grand Cherokee L and the long-wheelbase Range Rover. `ext_share` sets how many are the long version.

Each `pattern` is a regular expression for the DMV `make_model` field. It also catches the six-letter truncations found in older records ("CHEVROLET SUBURB").

```{r lengths}
lengths <- read_csv(len_file, show_col_types = FALSE)

lk <- lengths |>
  mutate(make_model = map(pattern, \(p) str_subset(unique(dmv$make_model), p))) |>
  unnest(make_model)

# Every pattern matches something, and no nameplate matches two different patterns
stopifnot(all(lengths$pattern %in% lk$pattern),
          !anyDuplicated(distinct(lk, pattern, make_model)$make_model))

new25 <- dmv |> filter(year == 2025)

# One row per DMV record x length row; `share` splits records between body lengths.
# Vehicles in `exempt` types pay nothing.
fee_rows <- function(data = new25, cap = Inf, body = "len", ext = ext_share, exempt = character(0)) {
  sizes <- lk |>
    mutate(share  = case_when(variant == "ext" ~ ext,
                              variant == "std" ~ 1 - ext,
                              .default = share),
           length = coalesce(.data[[body]], len),
           fee    = if_else(segment %in% exempt, 0, surcharge(length, cap))) |>
    select(make_model, my_from, my_to, segment, verified, share, length, fee)
  inner_join(data, sizes, by = join_by(make_model, between(model_year, my_from, my_to)),
             relationship = "many-to-many")
}
```

## 7. Revenue

Revenue scales the average surcharge among 2025 new registrations up to all `r format(stock, big.mark = ",")` vehicles, assuming the fleet's length mix matches the 2025 registrants'.

**Commercial vehicles.** The DMV file doesn't say which vehicles carry commercial plates, so the "commercial exempt" rows exempt commercial-type vehicles instead: the types listed in `commercial_types`. By default that is full-size vans (Transit, ProMaster, Express/Savana, E-Series, Sprinter, Metris, NV) and heavy-duty pickups (F-250/350/450, Ram 2500/3500). This exempts some personal vans and misses business-owned F-150s and Silverados. Most heavy trucks and buses are already out of the analysis: the DMV puts them in its "All Others" weight class, which both parts leave out.

```{r len_results}
summarise_fees <- function(r, data = new25) {
  r |> summarise(pct_charged     = 100 * sum(n * share * (fee > 0)) / sum(data$n),
                 fee_if_charged  = sum(n * share * fee) / sum(n * share * (fee > 0)),
                 fee_per_car     = sum(n * share * fee) / sum(data$n),
                 rev_2025_cars_M = sum(n * share * fee) / 1e6,
                 rev_fleet_M     = fee_per_car * stock / 1e6)
}

res <- bind_rows(
  "All vehicles, uncapped"      = summarise_fees(fee_rows()),
  "All vehicles, capped"        = summarise_fees(fee_rows(cap = fee_cap)),
  "Commercial exempt, uncapped" = summarise_fees(fee_rows(exempt = commercial_types)),
  "Commercial exempt, capped"   = summarise_fees(fee_rows(cap = fee_cap, exempt = commercial_types)),
  .id = "version")
res |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

```{r payer_median, include = FALSE}
# Weighted quantile: smallest x with at least share p of the weight at or below it
wquantile <- function(x, w, p) { o <- order(x); x[o][which(cumsum(w[o]) >= p * sum(w))[1]] }
payer_q <- function(r) {
  r0 <- filter(r, fee > 0)
  sapply(c(p50 = 0.5, p75 = 0.75, p90 = 0.9), \(p) round(wquantile(r0$fee, r0$n * r0$share, p)))
}
len_q <- payer_q(fee_rows())
```

About `r round(res$pct_charged[1])`% of vehicles are long enough to pay anything. The median payer owes $`r len_q["p50"]` a year (75th percentile $`r len_q["p75"]`, 90th percentile $`r len_q["p90"]`), and the average payer $`r round(res$fee_if_charged[1])`. Fleet-wide, the surcharge raises about **$`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[1], 1)` million a year uncapped, or $`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[2], 1)` million with a $`r fee_cap` cap**. Exempting commercial-type vehicles brings that to $`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[3], 1)` million uncapped, or $`r round(res$rev_fleet_M[4], 1)` million capped.

## Who pays

Vehicles charged and revenue by type, scaled to the full fleet. `commercial` marks the types exempted in the "commercial exempt" rows.

```{r len_segments}
by_segment <- function(r) {
  r |> group_by(segment) |>
    summarise(cars_charged = sum(n * share * (fee > 0)) / sum(new25$n) * stock,
              revenue_M    = sum(n * share * fee) / sum(new25$n) * stock / 1e6)
}

left_join(by_segment(fee_rows()),
          by_segment(fee_rows(cap = fee_cap)) |> select(segment, revenue_capped_M = revenue_M),
          by = "segment") |>
  mutate(avg_fee_uncapped = 1e6 * revenue_M / cars_charged,
         commercial       = segment %in% commercial_types) |>
  arrange(desc(revenue_M)) |>
  mutate(across(c(cars_charged, avg_fee_uncapped), round), across(starts_with("revenue"), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Sensitivity

Fleet revenue in $ millions.

```{r len_sensitivity}
run_len <- function(...) {
  r <- fee_rows(...)
  round(sum(r$n * r$share * r$fee) / sum(new25$n) * stock / 1e6, 2)
}

variants <- list("Central"                         = list(),
                 "Pickups and vans: shortest body" = list(body = "len_short"),
                 "Pickups and vans: longest body"  = list(body = "len_long"),
                 "No extended-length SUVs"         = list(ext = 0),
                 "Two-thirds extended-length SUVs" = list(ext = 2/3))

imap(variants, \(args, name) tibble(
  variant                    = name,
  uncapped_M                 = do.call(run_len, args),
  capped_M                   = do.call(run_len, c(args, cap = fee_cap)),
  uncapped_comm_exempt_M     = do.call(run_len, c(args, list(exempt = commercial_types))),
  capped_comm_exempt_M       = do.call(run_len, c(args, list(cap = fee_cap, exempt = commercial_types))))) |>
  list_rbind()
```

## Is 2025 a typical year?

Average surcharge per newly registered vehicle by registration year. Earlier files abbreviate more model names, so a few long vehicles go unmatched and older years read slightly low.

```{r len_by_year}
map(2019:2025, \(yr) {
  d <- filter(dmv, year == yr)
  tibble(year     = yr,
         uncapped = sum(with(fee_rows(d), n * share * fee)) / sum(d$n),
         capped   = sum(with(fee_rows(d, cap = fee_cap), n * share * fee)) / sum(d$n))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(across(c(uncapped, capped), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Caveats

* The estimate is static: it ignores any shift toward shorter vehicles.
* "Commercial" is a proxy based on vehicle type, not registration type (see section 7).
* Scaling 2025 registrations up to the fleet assumes the fleet's length mix matches recent registrants'. The table above suggests that mix has been stable since 2019.

# Part 3. An annual hood-height surcharge

This works like the length surcharge, with hood height in place of length. 
The surcharge is \$0 for a vehicle whose hood is no higher than `r H_low` in. Above that it rises 
`r if (hood_curve == 1) "in a straight line" else paste0("with the extra height raised to the power ", hood_curve)`, 
reaching \$`r hood_fee_at_esv` at `r H_high` in. and continuing upward beyond it. The "capped" results stop it at $`r hood_fee_cap`. It uses the same 2025 registrations, the same fleet scaling and the same commercial-type exemption as Part 2. The settings are in the `setup` chunk.

Hood height is the "hood leading edge": where a 1-meter straight edge, tilted 50° from vertical with its lower end 60 cm off the ground, first touches the front of the vehicle (the Euro NCAP / UN GTR 9 definition). The [IIHS](https://www.iihs.org/news/detail/vehicles-with-higher-more-vertical-front-ends-pose-greater-risk-to-pedestrians) found that vehicles with a hood leading edge more than 40 in. off the ground were 44–45% more likely to kill a pedestrian in a crash than vehicles with a hood 30 in. or lower and a sloped front.

## 8. The schedule

Heights below are from `hood_file`. `photo` is the carsized.com image measured, which shows the vehicle's generation.

```{r hood_schedule}
hood_fee <- function(h, cap = Inf, bottom = H_low, top = H_high) {
  pmin(hood_fee_at_esv * (pmax(h - bottom, 0) / (top - bottom))^hood_curve, cap)
}

norm <- function(x) str_to_upper(str_remove_all(str_squish(x), "-"))  # same as the DMV cleaning

hood <- read_excel(hood_file, sheet = "Hood_heights") |>
  select(rank = 1, nameplate = 2, hood_body = 3, hood_in = 4, page = 11) |>
  filter(!is.na(rank)) |>                                   # drops the notes under the table
  mutate(nameplate = recode(norm(nameplate), "JEEP WRANGLER UNLIMITED" = "JEEP WRANGLER"),
         photo     = str_extract(page, "cars/([^/]+)/", group = 1))

hood |>
  filter(nameplate %in% c("TESLA MODEL 3", "TOYOTA CAMRY", "HONDA CIVIC", "TESLA MODEL Y", "HONDA CRV",
                          "TOYOTA RAV4", "TOYOTA HIGHLANDER", "JEEP GRAND CHEROKEE", "CADILLAC ESCALADE",
                          "CHEVROLET TAHOE", "FORD F150", "CHEVROLET SILVERADO", "FORD BRONCO")) |>
  select(nameplate, hood_in, photo) |>
  add_row(nameplate = "Heavy-duty pickup (assumed)", hood_in = H_hd_pickup) |>
  mutate(uncapped = round(hood_fee(hood_in)),
         capped   = round(hood_fee(hood_in, cap = hood_fee_cap))) |>
  arrange(hood_in)
```

## 9. Hood heights

`hood_file` has hood heights for 195 of the 200 most common nameplates in DC's 2018–25 registrations, measured from carsized.com side photos scaled to each model's published height. Each nameplate is measured once, from the generation covering its median DC model year. The DMV records are matched to them with the same name cleaning as the earlier make-model analysis (`nameplate_harmonization.csv`).

Each 2025 vehicle then gets a height in this order:

* **Measured**: its nameplate was measured.
* **Borrowed**: a variant or twin of a measured nameplate (an M340i takes the 3 Series; a Lexus TX the Highlander), listed in `nameplate_harmonization_extra.csv`.
* **Imputed**: the weighted median measured height of 2025 vehicles of the same type. The type is the Part 2 segment if the vehicle is in `vehicle_lengths.csv`, and otherwise its body type from `body_type_lookup.csv` or `body_type_lookup_extra.csv`. Vehicles with no type get the median for measured vehicles that are not in the length table, i.e. no longer than a Camry.
* **Assumed**: heavy-duty pickups (none measured) get `H_hd_pickup`.
* **No hood**: motorcycles pay nothing.

A measurement error shared by every photo cancels out, because the fee depends only on how much higher a hood is than the Camry's. Errors that differ from model to model do not: across 32 models measured both ways, carsized.com photos typically read 1.7 in. higher than dimensions.com drawings, with a standard deviation of about 1.4 in. around that gap.

```{r hood_heights}
read_norm <- function(f) read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) |> mutate(across(everything(), norm))

harm_extra <- read_norm("nameplate_harmonization_extra.csv")
harm   <- bind_rows(read_norm("nameplate_harmonization.csv"), harm_extra) |>
  distinct(make_model, .keep_all = TRUE)
bodies <- bind_rows(read_csv("body_type_lookup.csv", show_col_types = FALSE),
                    read_csv("body_type_lookup_extra.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)) |>
  mutate(nameplate = norm(nameplate)) |>
  distinct(nameplate, .keep_all = TRUE)

# One row per nameplate, and every borrowed height points at a measured nameplate
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(hood$nameplate),
          all(harm_extra$nameplate %in% hood$nameplate[!is.na(hood$hood_in)]))

# Part 2 segments (one per make_model and model year) for vehicles longer than a Camry
seg_lookup <- fee_rows(dmv) |> distinct(make_model, model_year, len_segment = segment)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(select(seg_lookup, make_model, model_year)))

body_to_type <- c(Car = "Car", SUV = "Other SUV/crossover", Pickup = "Midsize pickup",
                  `Van/minivan` = "Minivan")

# Honda and BMW motorcycles (the only motorcycle makers among the brands kept): no hood
bike_pattern <- paste0("^BMW (R ?[0-9]|R NINE|K ?[0-9]|F ?[0-9]|S ?1000|C ?[0-9]|CE ?0|G ?[0-9]|M 1000)",
                       "|^HONDA (CB|CMX|CRF|CTX|GL1|GROM|NC7|NC750|NCH|NCW|NPS|NVA|PCX|VT|XR|Z125",
                       "|ADV|C125|CH|CN|CT125|WW|XL7)")

classify <- function(data) {
  data |>
    left_join(harm, by = "make_model") |>
    mutate(nameplate = coalesce(nameplate, make_model),
           borrowed  = make_model %in% harm_extra$make_model) |>
    left_join(select(hood, nameplate, hood_body, hood_in), by = "nameplate") |>
    left_join(bodies, by = "nameplate") |>
    left_join(seg_lookup, by = join_by(make_model, model_year)) |>
    mutate(segment = case_when(str_detect(coalesce(make_model, ""), bike_pattern) ~ "Motorcycle",
                               .default = coalesce(len_segment,
                                                   unname(body_to_type[coalesce(hood_body, body)]),
                                                   "Unclassified")))
}

# Fallback heights by type, from measured 2025 vehicles
measured25 <- classify(new25) |> filter(!is.na(hood_in))
type_in    <- measured25 |> summarise(type_in = wquantile(hood_in, n, 0.5), .by = segment)
short_in   <- with(filter(measured25, is.na(len_segment)), wquantile(hood_in, n, 0.5))

# One row per DMV record. `unmeasured` = "impute" (central), "zero" or "average"
# (unmeasured vehicles pay the average fee of measured ones).
hood_rows <- function(data = new25, cap = Inf, exempt = character(0), unmeasured = "impute",
                      bottom = H_low, top = H_high) {
  r <- classify(data) |>
    left_join(type_in, by = "segment") |>
    mutate(source = case_when(segment == "Motorcycle"        ~ "no hood",
                              !is.na(hood_in) & borrowed     ~ "borrowed",
                              !is.na(hood_in)                ~ "measured",
                              segment == "Heavy-duty pickup" ~ "assumed",
                              .default                       = "imputed"),
           height = case_when(source %in% c("measured", "borrowed") ~ hood_in,
                              source == "assumed"                   ~ H_hd_pickup,
                              source == "imputed"                   ~ coalesce(type_in, short_in)),
           fee    = if_else(source == "no hood", 0, hood_fee(height, cap, bottom, top)),
           share  = 1)                                      # so Part 2's helpers work unchanged
  known <- r$source %in% c("measured", "borrowed")
  paid  <- known & !r$segment %in% exempt
  if (unmeasured == "zero")    r$fee[!known] <- 0
  if (unmeasured == "average") r$fee[!known & r$source != "no hood"] <- weighted.mean(r$fee[paid], r$n[paid])
  mutate(r, fee = if_else(segment %in% exempt, 0, fee))
}

# Share of 2025 vehicles by where their height comes from, and the fallback heights used
hood_rows() |> count(source, wt = n) |> mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |> arrange(desc(n))
type_in |> add_row(segment = "Unclassified", type_in = short_in) |> arrange(type_in)
```

## 10. Revenue

```{r hood_results}
hres <- bind_rows(
  "All vehicles, uncapped"      = summarise_fees(hood_rows()),
  "All vehicles, capped"        = summarise_fees(hood_rows(cap = hood_fee_cap)),
  "Commercial exempt, uncapped" = summarise_fees(hood_rows(exempt = commercial_types)),
  "Commercial exempt, capped"   = summarise_fees(hood_rows(cap = hood_fee_cap, exempt = commercial_types)),
  .id = "version")
hres |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2)))

hood_q <- payer_q(hood_rows())
```

About `r round(hres$pct_charged[1])`% of vehicles have a hood higher than 
`r H_low` and pay something. The median payer owes 
\$`r hood_q["p50"]` a year 
(75th percentile \$`r hood_q["p75"]`, 90th percentile \$`r hood_q["p90"]`), and 
the average payer \$`r round(hres$fee_if_charged[1])`. 
Fleet-wide, the surcharge raises about **\$`r round(hres$rev_fleet_M[1], 1)` million a year uncapped, or \$`r round(hres$rev_fleet_M[2], 1)` million with a \$`r hood_fee_cap` cap**. 
Exempting commercial-type vehicles brings that to \$`r round(hres$rev_fleet_M[3], 1)` 
million uncapped, or \$`r round(hres$rev_fleet_M[4], 1)` million capped.

## Who pays

Vehicles charged and revenue by type, scaled to the full fleet. `pct_measured` is the share of each type's vehicles with a measured or borrowed height.

```{r hood_segments}
hr <- hood_rows()
left_join(by_segment(hr),
          by_segment(hood_rows(cap = hood_fee_cap)) |> select(segment, revenue_capped_M = revenue_M),
          by = "segment") |>
  left_join(hr |> summarise(pct_measured = 100 * sum(n[source %in% c("measured", "borrowed")]) / sum(n),
                            .by = segment), by = "segment") |>
  filter(cars_charged > 0) |>
  mutate(avg_fee_uncapped = 1e6 * revenue_M / cars_charged,
         commercial       = segment %in% commercial_types) |>
  arrange(desc(revenue_M)) |>
  mutate(across(c(cars_charged, avg_fee_uncapped, pct_measured), round),
         across(starts_with("revenue"), \(x) round(x, 2)))
```

## Sensitivity

Fleet revenue in \$ millions. The two anchor heights matter most: each is a single photo measurement, and moving the Camry's by an inch shifts the fee of nearly every vehicle by about \$`r round(hood_fee_at_esv / (H_high - H_low))`.

```{r hood_sensitivity}
run_hood <- function(...) {
  r <- hood_rows(...)
  round(sum(r$n * r$fee) / sum(new25$n) * stock / 1e6, 2)
}

hood_variants <- list("Central"                                   = list(),
                      "Unmeasured vehicles pay $0"                = list(unmeasured = "zero"),
                      "Unmeasured vehicles pay the average"       = list(unmeasured = "average"),
                      "Lower anchor 1 in. lower"                  = list(bottom = H_low - 1),
                      "Higher anchor 1 in. higher"                = list(bottom = H_low + 1),
                      "Escalade ESV anchor 47.8 in. (GMC Yukon)"  = list(top = 47.8))

hood_sens <- imap(hood_variants, \(args, name) tibble(
  variant                = name,
  uncapped_M             = do.call(run_hood, args),
  capped_M               = do.call(run_hood, c(args, cap = hood_fee_cap)),
  uncapped_comm_exempt_M = do.call(run_hood, c(args, list(exempt = commercial_types))),
  capped_comm_exempt_M   = do.call(run_hood, c(args, list(cap = hood_fee_cap, exempt = commercial_types))))) |>
  list_rbind()
hood_sens
```

## Is 2025 a typical year?

Average surcharge per newly registered vehicle by registration year. `pct_measured` falls in earlier years because their files abbreviate more model names.

```{r hood_by_year}
map(2019:2025, \(yr) {
  d  <- filter(dmv, year == yr)
  r  <- hood_rows(d)
  rc <- hood_rows(d, cap = hood_fee_cap)
  tibble(year         = yr,
         uncapped     = sum(r$n * r$fee) / sum(d$n),
         capped       = sum(rc$n * rc$fee) / sum(d$n),
         pct_measured = 100 * sum(r$n[r$source %in% c("measured", "borrowed")]) / sum(d$n))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  mutate(across(c(uncapped, capped, pct_measured), \(x) round(x, 1)))
```

## Caveats

* **One generation per nameplate.** Each nameplate's height comes from one photo, usually of the generation covering its median DC model year, and applies to every model year. The Escalade anchor is carsized.com's 2006 generation (2007–14 model years); the ESV shares its front end. The current Escalade may sit higher (see the sensitivity row using the Yukon's height). The Jeep Wrangler uses the 2007–17 JK (46.9 in.); a dimensions.com drawing of the 2018+ JL reads 4.3 in. lower, or about 2.6 in. after allowing for the usual gap between the two sources.
* **`r round(100 * sum(hr$n[hr$source %in% c("imputed", "assumed")]) / sum(hr$n))`% of 2025 vehicles have imputed or assumed heights.** Charging them nothing would cut uncapped revenue by $`r round(hood_sens$uncapped_M[1] - hood_sens$uncapped_M[2], 1)` million; charging them the measured vehicles' average fee instead of imputing changes it by $`r abs(round(hood_sens$uncapped_M[3] - hood_sens$uncapped_M[1], 1))` million.
* **Vans are probably overstated.** Every full-size van gets the Chevrolet Express's 47.9 in. The Transit, ProMaster and Sprinter weren't measured, and their short, sloped noses probably sit lower. The commercial-exempt rows remove them.
* The estimate is static and the commercial exemption is a proxy, as in Part 2.

# Checks

```{r checks}
# 1. The lognormal formula matches a simulation
set.seed(1)
mu  <- c(30000, 50000, 90000)
sim <- sapply(mu, \(m) mean(pmax(rlnorm(1e6, log(m) - spread^2 / 2, spread) - threshold, 0)))
round(rbind(formula = expected_excess(mu), simulation = sim))

# 2. Honda and BMW motorcycles are valued as if they were cars in Part 1
bikes <- str_detect(coalesce(dmv$make_model, ""), bike_pattern)   # pattern defined in section 9
c(bikes_still_registered = round(sum(dmv$still_here[bikes])),
  tax_M = round(sum(dmv$still_here[bikes] * dmv$tax[bikes]) / 1e6, 2),
  pct_of_revenue = round(100 * sum(dmv$still_here[bikes] * dmv$tax[bikes]) / sum(dmv$still_here * dmv$tax), 1))

# 3. Share of the 2025 length revenue that rests on lengths checked against
#    manufacturer, dealer or KBB spec pages ("web") vs. the autoevolution dataset or approximations
r <- fee_rows()
r |> group_by(verified) |>
  summarise(pct_of_uncapped_revenue = round(100 * sum(n * share * fee) / sum(r$n * r$share * r$fee), 1))


# 5. Share of the 2025 hood revenue by where the height comes from
hr |> group_by(source) |>
  summarise(pct_of_vehicles         = round(100 * sum(n) / sum(hr$n), 1),
            pct_of_uncapped_revenue = round(100 * sum(n * fee) / sum(hr$n * hr$fee), 1))
```

# Sources

* Prices: [KBB average transaction prices, October 2026](https://www.coxautoinc.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/October-2026-Kelley-Blue-Book-Average-Transaction-Price-tables.pdf); [KBB depreciation rates](https://www.kbb.com/car-depreciation).
* Anchor lengths: [2025 Camry, 193.5 in. (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/toyota/camry/2025/specs); [2025 Escalade ESV, 227 in. (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/cadillac/escalade-esv/2025/specs).
* Main pickups and vans: [Ford F-150 spec sheet](https://media.ford.com/content/dam/fordmedia/North%20America/US/product/2024/f150/2024%20Ford%20F-150%20Tech%20Specs.pdf); [Ford Transit spec sheet](https://www.fromtheroad.ford.com/content/dam/fordmediasite/us/en/library/2025/specs/2025%20Ford%20Transit%20Technical%20Specifications.pdf); [Chevrolet Express](https://chevrolet.com/commercial/express/vans); [Ram ProMaster (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/ram/promaster/2020/specs/); [Silverado (GM Authority)](https://gmauthority.com/blog/2026/10/2027-chevy-silverado-1500-vs-2026-silverado-1500-exterior-dimensions-compared/); [Ram 1500](https://www.glendaledodgecalifornia.com/research-ram-1500-cabs-boxes.html); [Tundra](https://pickuptrucktalk.com/2021/10/is-the-2022-toyota-tundra-smaller-a-spec-by-spec-comparison/); [Sprinter](https://www.mercedesbenzofwarwick.com/2024-mercedes-benz-sprinter-dimensions/); [E-Series](https://vandimensions.com/database/ford/e-series-2008).
* Large SUVs and minivans: [Tahoe and Suburban](https://www.automotive-fleet.com/news/chevrolet-refreshes-2021-tahoe-and-suburban-suvs); [Escalade generations (GM Authority)](https://gmauthority.com/blog/gm/cadillac/escalade/escalade-esv/); [Yukon](https://www.truedelta.com/GMC-Yukon/specs-103-2021); [Expedition spec sheet](https://www.fromtheroad.ford.com/content/dam/fordmediasite/us/en/library/2025/specs/2025-Ford-Expedition-Technical-Specs.pdf); [minivans (KBB)](https://www.kbb.com/compare-cars/results/van-minivan).
* Other lengths: the [autoevolution specs dataset](https://github.com/ilyasozkurt/automobile-models-and-specs) where it has the U.S. model; the rest are marked "approx" in the CSV.
* Hood heights: measured from [carsized.com](https://www.carsized.com) side photos (pages listed in `hood_file`), cross-checked against [dimensions.com](https://www.dimensions.com) drawings for 32 models. Pedestrian risk: [IIHS (2023)](https://www.iihs.org/news/detail/vehicles-with-higher-more-vertical-front-ends-pose-greater-risk-to-pedestrians). Heavy-duty pickups: [Consumer Reports](https://www.consumerreports.org/cars/car-safety/the-hidden-dangers-of-big-trucks-a9662450602/) measured the front edge of some heavy-duty hoods, such as the Ford F-250's, at 55 in. or more.
